name: United States
summary: The world's largest economy and pre-eminent military power, with a global network of treaty allies and bases. US strategy centres on competition with China, energy and technology leadership, and a more transactional, tariff-driven approach to trade and alliance burden-sharing.
strategicInterests: Maintain military and technological primacy over China, especially in semiconductors and AI
Preserve deterrence in the Indo-Pacific (Taiwan Strait, South China Sea, Korean Peninsula)
Reshore strategic manufacturing and use tariffs as leverage in trade negotiations
Energy dominance as the world's largest oil and gas producer
Western Hemisphere security: migration, narcotics trafficking and Venezuela

government.notes: Bicameral Congress; Republican control of both chambers after the 2024 election.

resources.name: Shale oil & gas
resources.note: Largest producer of both crude oil and natural gas; top LNG exporter

resources.name: Farmland
resources.note: Leading exporter of soybeans, corn and wheat

resources.name: Rare earths
resources.note: Mountain Pass mine; processing capacity being rebuilt with federal support

resources.name: Lithium & copper
resources.note: Large undeveloped deposits (Thacker Pass, Resolution Copper)

name: Canada
summary: A resource superpower tightly integrated with the US economy — roughly three-quarters of its exports go south. US tariffs and annexation rhetoric in 2025 pushed Ottawa to diversify trade, accelerate defence spending and assert Arctic sovereignty.
strategicInterests: Reduce dependence on the US market and secure the 2026 USMCA review
Arctic sovereignty, including the Northwest Passage
NORAD modernisation and reaching the NATO 2% target
Build critical-mineral supply chains with allies

government.notes: Liberal minority government since the April 2025 election.

resources.name: Oil sands
resources.note: Third-largest proven oil reserves globally

resources.name: Potash
resources.note: World's largest producer

resources.name: Uranium
resources.note: Athabasca Basin — among the highest-grade deposits in the world

resources.name: Critical minerals
resources.note: Nickel, cobalt, graphite and lithium

resources.name: Freshwater
resources.note: Around 7% of the world's renewable freshwater

name: Mexico
summary: The United States' largest trading partner and a key beneficiary of nearshoring. Mexico's agenda is dominated by managing Washington — tariffs, migration and cartel violence — while defending its economic model ahead of the USMCA review.
strategicInterests: Protect USMCA market access and attract nearshoring investment
Contain cartel violence while limiting unilateral US security action
Manage northbound migration flows
Revive state energy champions (Pemex, CFE)

government.notes: Morena holds a supermajority in Congress; 2024 judicial reform introduced elected judges.

resources.name: Silver
resources.note: World's largest producer

resources.name: Oil
resources.note: State-controlled via Pemex; output in long decline

resources.name: Lithium
resources.note: Nationalised in 2022

resources.name: Manufacturing corridors
resources.note: Border and Bajío industrial clusters integrated with US supply chains

name: Brazil
summary: Latin America's largest economy and an agricultural superpower that positions itself as a leader of the Global South. Brazil pursues strategic autonomy through BRICS while remaining a pivotal voice on climate, hosting COP30 in Belém in 2025.
strategicInterests: Leadership of the Global South and reform of global governance (UNSC seat)
Amazon protection and climate diplomacy
Expand agricultural and energy exports, especially to Asia
Regional integration via Mercosur, including the EU–Mercosur agreement

capabilities: Largest armed forces in Latin America

government.notes: Fragmented Congress; general election due October 2026.

resources.name: Pre-salt oil
resources.note: Deep-water fields make Brazil a top-10 crude producer

resources.name: Iron ore
resources.note: Second-largest exporter (Vale)

resources.name: Niobium
resources.note: Around 90% of world supply

resources.name: Rare earths
resources.note: Among the largest reserves outside China

resources.name: Amazon rainforest
resources.note: Largest tropical forest; central to climate negotiations

name: Argentina
summary: A resource-rich economy undergoing radical libertarian shock therapy under President Milei, who has aligned Buenos Aires closely with Washington. Inflation has fallen sharply from triple digits, backed by a new IMF programme and US financial support.
strategicInterests: Macroeconomic stabilisation and a return to international capital markets
Develop Vaca Muerta shale and lithium for export
Close alignment with the United States and Israel
Sovereignty claim over the Falklands/Malvinas

government.notes: Milei's party strengthened its position in the October 2025 midterm elections.

resources.name: Vaca Muerta shale
resources.note: Second-largest shale gas and fourth-largest shale oil resources

resources.name: Lithium
resources.note: Part of the Lithium Triangle with Chile and Bolivia

resources.name: Pampas farmland
resources.note: Top exporter of soybean meal and oil

name: Chile
summary: The world's largest copper producer and a major lithium supplier, making it central to the energy transition. A stable, open economy with dense trade links to China and the Pacific.
strategicInterests: Capture more value from copper and lithium (national lithium strategy)
Pacific trade diversification (CPTPP, China, US)
Antarctic territorial claim and southern maritime routes

government.notes: Presidential election held late 2025; new administration takes office March 2026.

resources.name: Copper
resources.note: Roughly a quarter of world mine output

resources.name: Lithium
resources.note: Second-largest producer (Atacama salt flat)

resources.name: Fisheries & fruit
resources.note: Leading exporter of salmon and cherries

name: Colombia
summary: A long-standing US security partner whose left-wing government has pursued 'total peace' talks with armed groups while clashing with Washington over drug policy and migration. Coca cultivation and armed-group violence remain high.
strategicInterests: Negotiated settlements with ELN and FARC dissident groups
Rethink counter-narcotics policy
Manage the Venezuelan border and migrant population
Energy transition away from oil and coal

government.notes: Presidential election due May 2026; Petro is term-limited.

resources.name: Oil & coal
resources.note: Largest export earners

resources.name: Coffee
resources.note: Third-largest producer

resources.name: Emeralds & gold
resources.note: Significant artisanal and illegal mining

resources.name: Biodiversity
resources.note: Second most biodiverse country

name: Venezuela
summary: Holder of the world's largest proven oil reserves, hollowed out by economic collapse, sanctions and emigration of nearly 8 million people. The disputed 2024 election deepened isolation, and a large US naval build-up in the Caribbean in late 2025 sharply escalated tensions.
strategicInterests: Regime survival under US pressure and sanctions
Sustain oil exports via licences and shadow-fleet sales to Asia
Assert the claim to Guyana's Essequibo region
Security and economic ties with Russia, China, Iran and Cuba

capabilities: Russian-supplied Su-30 fighters and S-300 air defences

government.notes: The July 2024 election result is disputed; the opposition and many governments say Edmundo González won.

resources.name: Oil
resources.note: ~300 billion barrels of proven reserves, mostly extra-heavy Orinoco crude

resources.name: Natural gas
resources.note: Largest reserves in Latin America

resources.name: Gold & coltan
resources.note: Orinoco Mining Arc, much of it informal or illicit

name: Cuba
summary: A one-party communist state in deep economic crisis, marked by repeated nationwide blackouts, food shortages and mass emigration. It remains under a comprehensive US embargo and relies on Russia, China, Venezuela and Mexico for fuel and credit.
strategicInterests: Regime continuity and economic survival
Secure fuel supplies and restore the electrical grid
Easing of the US embargo and removal from the state-sponsors-of-terrorism list
Deepen ties with Russia and China

capabilities: Intelligence ties with Russia and China

government.notes: Communist Party of Cuba is constitutionally the leading force of state and society.

resources.name: Nickel & cobalt
resources.note: Among the largest nickel reserves; Sherritt joint venture

resources.name: Tourism
resources.note: Leading hard-currency earner, still below pre-pandemic levels

name: Peru
summary: A major copper, silver and gold producer with chronically unstable politics — it has had seven presidents since 2016. The Chinese-built Chancay megaport, opened in 2024, is reshaping South American–Asian trade routes.
strategicInterests: Expand mining output and investment
Leverage Chancay port as a Pacific logistics hub
Restore political stability ahead of the 2026 elections

government.notes: Became president in October 2025 after Congress removed Dina Boluarte; general election due April 2026.

resources.name: Copper
resources.note: Second- or third-largest producer

resources.name: Silver & gold
resources.note: Top-three silver producer

resources.name: Chancay port
resources.note: COSCO-operated deep-water port opened November 2024

name: Guyana
summary: The world's fastest-growing economy thanks to offshore oil discoveries in the Stabroek block. Its oil wealth has intensified Venezuela's claim over the Essequibo region, which makes up about two-thirds of Guyana's territory.
strategicInterests: Defend territorial integrity against Venezuela's Essequibo claim
Manage the oil boom and sovereign wealth fund
Deepen security ties with the US and Caribbean partners

capabilities: Growing US and UK training support

government.system: Unitary parliamentary republic with executive president

resources.name: Offshore oil
resources.note: Stabroek block: 11+ billion barrels discovered (ExxonMobil-led)

resources.name: Gold & bauxite
resources.note: Traditional mainstays of the economy
